BLOCKING FINDINGS.

F1. AN UNREADABLE EVENT PAYLOAD SILENTLY ESCALATES A TARGETED RUN INTO A REPO-WIDE SWEEP. THIS IS MINE AND IS IN NEITHER EXISTING RECORD, AND I CONSIDER IT THE WORST THING IN THE DIFF.
emit_find_prs does:
    event_path = os.environ.get("GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")
    event = {}
    if event_path:
        try: event = json.load(...)
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            print(f"NOTICE: could not read GITHUB_EVENT_PATH: {exc}")
            event = {}
    numbers = resolve_pr_numbers(event)
`{}` is not an error value in resolve_pr_numbers -- it is the DELIBERATE ENCODING OF "this is the schedule sweep, take every open PR targeting main". So "I could not read the event" and "this is the scheduled sweep" share one representation, which is this repository's own named defect pattern (HANDOFF item 5), and here it does not fail safe -- it fails LOUD AND WIDE. Measured against the real script and the live API:
    $ env -u GITHUB_EVENT_PATH python scripts/cloud/auto_queue.py --find-prs
    prs=45,44,43,40
    exit 0                          <- no notice of any kind
    $ GITHUB_EVENT_PATH="" ...      -> prs=45,44,43,40   exit 0, no notice
    $ GITHUB_EVENT_PATH=/nonexistent ...
    NOTICE: could not read GITHUB_EVENT_PATH: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
    prs=45,44,43,40                 exit 0
    $ GITHUB_EVENT_PATH=<file containing 'not json'> ...
    NOTICE: could not read GITHUB_EVENT_PATH: Expecting value: line 1 column 1
    prs=45,44,43,40                 exit 0
So a workflow_dispatch naming ONE pull request, or a workflow_run naming ONE head sha, degrades on an unset/empty/corrupt event file into "attempt to enqueue every open pull request in the repository" -- and in the unset and empty-string cases with NO diagnostic at all, because the `if event_path:` guard skips the try/except that would have printed one. The next step's guard is `if: steps.find.outputs.prs != ''`, which a four-PR sweep passes, so nothing downstream stops it; only `_all_required_checks_green` does, per PR, which is a readiness check and not an authorisation check. The old inline heredoc this replaced could not do this: with no check_suite key it printed `prs=` and stopped.
This is untested. PROBE: I changed the except branch to print `prs=` and return instead of falling through to the sweep -> 532 passed, 0 failed. Nothing in the suite pins the current behaviour either way.
The fix is small and belongs in this PR: give resolve_pr_numbers an explicit event-name argument (GITHUB_EVENT_NAME is always set in Actions) or have emit_find_prs return None -> `prs=` on an unreadable payload, so the sweep is reachable only from an event that really is `schedule`.

F2. THE NEW STEP WRITES DIAGNOSTICS INTO $GITHUB_OUTPUT, AND THE DOCSTRING'S STATED FAILURE BEHAVIOUR IS FALSE. Independently found, and it agrees with both existing records. The step is `run: python scripts/cloud/auto_queue.py --find-prs >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` -- every byte of stdout lands in the output file -- and every NOTICE in this script goes to stdout, not stderr. Measured exactly:
    $ GITHUB_EVENT_PATH=<{"inputs":{"pr_number":"not-a-number"}}> python scripts/cloud/auto_queue.py --find-prs 2>/dev/null | cat -A
    NOTICE: could not resolve pull requests for this event$
    prs=$
Line 1 contains no '=' and is not a heredoc delimiter, so it is not a valid GITHUB_OUTPUT file command. `_api`'s own NOTICE is worse in the other direction -- it embeds the failing URL, which CONTAINS '=' ('...pulls?state=open&base=main...'), so it parses as an output whose name is everything up to the first '=' instead of failing outright. Either way emit_find_prs's own docstring -- "A lookup failure prints prs= (empty) rather than failing the job: this workflow retries every 15 minutes ... so a transient API failure here should not need a human" -- is not what the shipped step does. The heredoc this replaced printed only `prs=...` and had neither problem, so this is a regression introduced on the exact retry/self-heal path the PR is sold on.
HONEST SCOPE, SAME LIMIT BOTH OTHER REVIEWERS DECLARED: I did not execute a GitHub Actions runner; I cannot from this container. What I measured is the script's exact stdout on four failure paths and the workflow's exact redirect. That those lines are invalid GITHUB_OUTPUT commands follows from the documented name=value / heredoc format, not from watching a runner reject them. One line fixes it: file=sys.stderr on every NOTICE.

F3. THE DELIVERABLE ITSELF -- THE TRIGGER CHANGE -- IS COMPLETELY UNTESTED, AND I PROBED HARDER THAN 'REVERT IT'. Three mutations of .github/workflows/auto-queue.yml, each run against the full suite:
    (A) revert `on:` to the old `check_suite: types: [completed]`, i.e. restore the exact defect this PR exists to fix -> 532 passed, 0 failed.
    (B) point workflow_run at names that do not exist ("Continuous Integration", "Hand-off") -> 532 passed, 0 failed.
    (C) replace the whole find step with `run: echo "prs=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`, disconnecting auto_queue.py from the workflow entirely -> 532 passed, 0 failed.
(C) is the one that should worry a reader: all 10 new tests can pass while the script they test is not invoked by anything. tests/test_workflows_parse.py, which proof/44.json cites as evidence the workflow is valid, parses the YAML and asserts nothing about `on:` or about the step's command, so it is green under all three. A parse-level assertion -- that auto-queue.yml's `on:` keys are exactly {workflow_run, schedule, workflow_dispatch}, that workflow_run.workflows are names some workflow in .github/workflows actually declares, and that the find step invokes auto_queue.py --find-prs -- is cheap, is the only thing that would have caught V2 had it been wrong, and would make all three probes red.

NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS.

N1. A SIBLING FIELD THAT CHANGES THE MEANING IS IGNORED. The trigger is `workflow_run: types: [completed]`, which fires for conclusion 'failure', 'cancelled' and 'skipped' exactly as it does for 'success'. resolve_pr_numbers reads `workflow_run["head_sha"]` and never `workflow_run["conclusion"]` (or `name`). Measured:
    GITHUB_EVENT_PATH=<{"workflow_run":{"head_sha":"ee216c9...","conclusion":"failure","name":"CI"}}> --find-prs -> prs=44
A failed CI run therefore drives a full resolve-and-enqueue attempt. `_all_required_checks_green` stops it from doing harm, so this is wasted API calls and log noise rather than a merge-safety defect -- which is why it is not blocking -- but it is the read-one-field-ignore-the-sibling shape, and `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` on the job is one line.

N2. THE SCHEDULED SWEEP TURNS A DELIBERATELY LOUD FAILURE INTO A PERMANENT ONE. 'Require the AUTO_TOKEN_QUEUE secret' runs whenever prs is non-empty and exits 1 when the secret is unset -- correct, and deliberately so. But the sweep makes prs non-empty every 15 minutes for as long as any PR is open, so an unset secret becomes ~96 failing runs a day rather than one failure at the moment someone asked for a merge. I could NOT determine whether AUTO_TOKEN_QUEUE is set: I cannot read secrets, the three historical runs are all 'success' but I cannot read their logs (see WHAT I DID NOT CHECK), and a success is equally consistent with the secret being present or with `prs` having been empty and the step skipped. Recording it as a scheduling consequence to decide deliberately, not as a defect.

N3. `if "--find-prs" in sys.argv` matches the flag anywhere in argv, including after a `--` separator or as a value. Harmless today (nothing else passes arguments), noted only so it is not rediscovered.
